Using a Q4-birth indicator as the instrument for years of schooling, with year-of-birth and state-of-birth dummies as controls, each extra year of schooling is associated with about an 8.53% higher wage.

I ran the IV (two-stage least squares) estimate by partialling the controls out of the instrument, schooling and log wage, then taking the ratio of the instrument–wage covariance to the instrument–schooling covariance. The first attempt with a full dummy-variable matrix ran out of memory, so I used this equivalent route. The IV coefficient on schooling is 0.0853.

ANSWER: 8.53%
